summary: 5xx wave after weighted-route rewrite caused HTTP/2 stream-slot leak and upstream runtime crashes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightCart) experienced an abrupt spike in 5xx responses on several streaming and short-request endpoints beginning ~2026-03-10 08:12 UTC after a weighted-route rewrite was deployed to shift traffic between model variants. The API gateway returned 502/503s and a subset of upstream runtime pods crashed with SIGABRT / runtime OOM messages.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx for ~18 minutes across multiple customers in us-east-1, notably BrightCart (dedicated capacity).
- Streaming sessions dropped with 'stream reset' errors, and short synchronous text-generation calls received 502s.
- Customer impact: degraded UX on live checkout assistant; BrightCart reported failed requests and increased latency spikes.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-east) 
- Affected services: api-gateway (http2 frontend), serving-runtime (model-serving pods on dedicated GPU pool), ingress-prioritizer (weighted route controller).
- Recent change: rollout of "weighted-route rewrite" to shift 20% of traffic to quantized variant (2026-03-10 08:05 UTC).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Use short-payload synchronous requests with priority header set to 'interactive' while the weighted-route controller is in the middle of an update.
2) Open multiple long-lived streaming connections (chat sessions) simultaneously and maintain keepalive.
3) Observe api-gateway metrics: accept-queue depth grows, http2 active streams approaches configured max, and new connections begin to get 502/503.

Observed logs / snippets:
- apigw: "WARN http2: active_streams=240 max_concurrent_streams=250 accept_queue=512"
- apigw: "ERROR route: rewrite applied, recalculating weights -> delayed socket handoffs"
- runtime pod: "fatal error: runtime: out of memory" (several pods)
- runtime: "panic: net/http: connection closed by peer while writing response"
- kernel: "oom-killer invoked for process /srv/runtime/bin/worker"

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled back weighted-route rewrite at 08:18 UTC (immediate mitigation).
- Increased apigw http2 max_concurrent_streams soft-limit from 250 -> 400 for the us-east apigw pool to provide breathing room.
- Enabled short-term keepalive pruning on the apigw to reclaim half-open sockets.

Notes on customer communication:
- BrightCart notified at 08:25 UTC that we had detected the issue, actions were taken, and rollback was in progress. They confirmed partial recovery at 08:34 UTC.
- Customer asked for postmortem and whether variant rollouts can be throttled differently for dedicated customers.
comments: Support: 2026-03-10 08:22 UTC - triaged by Asha: rolling back weighted-route rewrite and notifying SRE; elevated error rate confirmed via dashboards (5xx rate from 0.8% -> 12%).

SRE (Ethan): 2026-03-10 08:27 UTC - Observed accept-queue and http2 stream saturation. Found a correlation between the timing of the route rewrite and a spike in half-open streams (SYN_SENT/SYN_RECV). Attaching pcap and metrics pointers in GH ticket.

Customer (BrightCart): 2026-03-10 08:36 UTC - Confirmed that errors reduced after rollback but saw residual latency for ~10 minutes. Requested a timeline for permanent fix. Provided sample request IDs: rq_3b9f2a, rq_3b9f8c.

SRE (Ethan): 2026-03-11 10:12 UTC - Investigation shows an http2 stream-slot accounting bug in apigw when routes are reweighted rapidly; the code path that transfers accept-queue ownership to new worker occasionally leaves slots marked as 'in-use' without active stream objects. This slowly exhausts the available concurrent_streams count and triggers backpressure to upstream runtimes, causing prefetch thrash and eventual OOMs.

Support: 2026-03-12 09:05 UTC - Notified BrightCart of intended mitigation: throttle route-rewrite rollouts to 5% per minute for dedicated customers and schedule permanent patch during low-traffic window.
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: 08:05-08:12 UTC window shows http2_active_streams jump +360% and accept_queue growth from 32 -> 512 across 3 apigw instances.
dmesg on runtime pods shows repeated allocations then OOM; memory growth correlated with multiple failed prefetch retries (kvcache fingerprints increasing).
tcpdump indicates many FIN/ACK pairs followed by RSTs around the same time as the rewrite; suggests sockets were torn down mid-handshake during weight recalculation.

Heap profiles on runtime pods (captured pre-oom) show increased goroutine counts stuck in Write loop waiting on net.Conn that returned EOFs. Hypothesis: apigw marked streams as 'occupied' but closed underlying conn -> runtime kept buffers and retried prefetch/kv operations until memory exhausted.
Config review: weighted-route controller allowed immediate weight commit; no staging gradual step for dedicated tenants.
resolution:
Status: Partial mitigation deployed (rollback of rewrite + increased http2 soft limits + keepalive pruning) restored service for BrightCart. Root cause: http2 stream-slot leak in apigw triggered by rapid weighted-route changes; leak propagated backpressure to serving runtimes causing memory growth and crashes.

Immediate next steps:
- Ship hotfix PR to apigw that fixes stream-slot accounting (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5421 in review).
- Implement rollout throttling for weighted-route changes: default 5% per minute for dedicated/private tenants; allow opt-in fast rollouts with explicit approval.
- Add a safety circuit: if apigw accept_queue or active_streams > 75% for 30s, pause route reweight operations and surface alert to SRE.
- Postmortem: schedule Confluence postmortem doc and runbook update; assign follow-up INT ticket to track permanent guardrails.

Follow-up items: 
- INT-2201 (apigw http2 slot accounting deeper audit)
- INFRA-PR-5421 (hotfix -> canary -> prod rollouts)
- Confluence runbook update link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/accept-queue-drainplaybook
resolution_status: Mitigation applied; patch in code review; monitoring/guardrails planned
